subject: Mechanical Engineering
title: Power in Fluid Systems
description: A quick win: understand Power in Fluid Systems.

hook.text: Hydraulic power equals pressure times flow rate. Double either one and you double the power delivered.

buildup.text: A pump converts mechanical energy into fluid power. The motor or engine driving the pump sets the input.

discovery.text: Typical hydraulic systems run at 150 to 250 bar. Pressure that high packs enormous power into small cylinders.

twist.text: Efficiency is never 100%. Friction in valves and hoses converts some power to heat. The oil warms up.

climax.text: A compact hydraulic system delivers more power per kilogram than almost any other technology. That's why planes use it.

punchline.text: Pressure times flow equals power. Small pipes, huge force.

quiz.question: Why do aircraft prefer hydraulic systems for flight controls?
options: Hydraulic fluid weighs less than any other power transmission medium
Hydraulic systems deliver more power per kilogram than most alternatives
Hydraulic systems never fail, making them the safest option available
